text: Functions are how you stop repeating yourself. This lesson covers defining them, giving them default values, and the calling style real AI SDKs expect.
def starts the definition, parentheses hold the parameters, and return sends a value back. A function with no return statement just returns None.
A parameter can have a default, making it optional. Call with just the prompt and both defaults apply; override just one by naming it.
You can pass arguments by name instead of position. This is exactly how real AI SDKs expect calls to look — naming arguments makes a call self-documenting and order-independent.
*args collects any number of extra positional arguments; **kwargs collects any number of extra named ones. This is how libraries like requests accept a flexible set of options.
Functions package logic; next lesson covers what happens when that logic fails — error handling with try and except, so one bad API call doesn't crash your whole program.
